To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the main factors affecting the content of lipoxydase pathway volatile compounds in EVOO are the temperature and the cultivar, while the factors affecting the content in carotenoids are the temperature and ripeness.
malaxation temperature has the greatest impact on volatile compounds, whereas malaxation time is the factor with the greatest impact on the content of phenolic compounds.
the malaxation process has a great influence on the content of volatile and pigment compounds in olive oil.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the optimization of the extraction process to obtain EVOOs with different sensory profiles, according to the desired quality of the EVOO.
the effect of the malaxation conditions on the quality of EVOO obtained from the three most common cultivars grown in the Mediterranean basin.
a study of the influence of the three factors on the quality of EVOO from three different cultivars.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
malaxation time and temperature have a strong influence on the quality and the sensory characteristics of EVOO.

the best EVOO is the one obtained from the Arbequinas, Koroneiki or Arbosanas cultivars, from rainfed crops and from olive samples with a lower degree of ripeness, with a malaxation temperature of 25 °C and with a malaxing time of 45 min.

the EVOOs obtained from the Koroneki cultivar and from olive samples with a lower degree of ripening, and from rainfed olive crops, have a higher content of pigments, whereas EVOOs obtained with a lower malaxation temperature and from irrigated olive crops, and from the Arboasana cultivar, had the highest volatile compound contents.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the malaxation time, the diameter of the grid of the hammer-crushing machine, and the cultivar have the most influence on olive oil quality.
the EVOO from Arbequina cultivars and from irrigated crops had a higher content of volatile compounds, while EVOO from Koroneiki cultivars had a higher content in pigments.
the malaxation time and the malaxation temperatures have an influence on the content of lipoxygense volatile compounds and the content of pigments, respectively.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the content of volatile and pigment compounds in EVOO can be modulated by the extraction process.
EVOO obtained from Arbequina cultivars, at the beginning of ripening, and from irrigated crops, with malaxation temperature at 25–28 °C and malaxation for 30–45 min, is recommended.
